register: consumer census of a public 15-minute news-data file infrastructure
what_a_row_means: one publicly distributed package whose source was obtained from a package registry itself and read by hand. Every cell that names a behaviour carries a file-and-line citation into the fetched source, at the exact version named in 'version'. Behaviour cells are statements about that version's code as read on 2026-08-10; only the two rows marked executed:true were also run.

populations.P-A: public Python package index, complete project-name list from its own simple endpoint (867935 names, HTTP 200, 2026-08-10), screened case-insensitively for the token in the package NAME. Exhaustive over names; blind to any package that consumes the object without naming it.
populations.P-B: R archive network: complete current-package descriptor database (24719 packages) screened over Package+Title+Description -> 0 hits; plus the archive directory of withdrawn packages (27546 directories) screened by name -> 1 hit.

not_covered: code distributed only through source hosting and not through a registry
packages consuming the object without the token in their name (P-A) or metadata (P-B)
notebooks, scripts and pipelines that fetch the files directly with a generic HTTP client

rows.consumes: v2 15-minute series; also offers a warehouse route
rows.C2_note: the master list publishes an MD5 beside every entry; the only hashing in the package is sha256 over cache keys (src/py_gdelt/cache.py:329,335)
rows.C3_on_a_listed_but_absent_file: 404 raises APIError inside the download layer; the fetcher's error policy decides and the DEFAULT is 'warn'. The package DOES have a partial-failure container (FetchResult: data / failed / complete / partial / total_failed, py_gdelt/models/common.py) — but on execution the container did not fire: see executed_result.
rows.C3_verbatim_comment_in_source: # Missing files are normal (not all 15-min slots exist)  [src/py_gdelt/sources/files.py:311]
rows.executed_result: Asked for the whole of 2022-11-11 (events, date range start=end=the day) through the package's own async entry point: FetchResult with 0 records, complete=True, total_failed=0, no exception. Control 2022-11-09: 2,668 records, complete=True, total_failed=0. Diagnostic (diagnose-gdelt-py.json): for a whole-day range the package requests exactly ONE cycle per stream (00:00:00), not 96; on the outage day both of those requests returned 404 (2 'File not found (404)' log lines) and NONE of them reached the failed list. So a result object designed to report partial failure reported a complete result with zero failures on a day where every file it asked for was absent.
executed_caveats: The control day's 2,668 records are far fewer than the 116,317 the two other clients return for the same day, because this package requested one cycle rather than 96. That per-day/per-cycle behaviour is a separate matter this session did not diagnose further and makes no claim about.

The package's documented synchronous entry point (events.query_sync) raised RuntimeError('Event loop is closed') on both windows in this environment; the async entry point was used. Recorded, not diagnosed.

standing_conditions: Every behaviour cell describes the exact version named in the row, as distributed by the registry on 2026-08-10. A later release may behave differently.
Only two rows were executed. The rest are readings of source code, and are labelled as such.

This is not a defect report about any maintainer's competence. Two of the seven fetching packages verify the published checksum and one returns incompleteness as a value; the census records that as prominently as the rest.
No claim is made about why any file is absent, in either direction.
